review_candidates.title: Building Enclosure Senior Project Associate
review_candidates.description: ECS is seeking a Building Enclosure Senior Project Associate to join our Southeast Building Science + Infrastructure team in Memphis, TN . In this role, you will manage building enclosure consulting projects and serve as a lead technical consultant on building enclosure investigations, assessments, commissioning, testing, and design consulting. You will work closely with clients and multidisciplinary project teams to evaluate building envelope performance, support construction quality, and deliver practical consulting solutions across a variety of facility types. This is a client-facing role with daily interaction with clients, architects, contractors, engineers, and owners. The position involves significant responsibility for project management, technical execution, and mentorship of junior staff within a collaborative consulting environment. Responsibilities Technical & Field Work Perform building science & infrastructure related testing, inspections, and consulting services. Conduct site observations and inspections of roofing and building enclosure systems. Interpret drawings, figures, and site plans; perform drafting or CAD work as needed. Develop testing plans and perform specialized building enclosure testing. Interpret test results, identify deficiencies, and recommend corrective actions. Perform building enclosure investigations, forensic assessments, and commissioning (BECx). Perform new construction design reviews and design of repairs to existing building envelope components. Perform peer review of design documents, specifications, and submittals. Maintain knowledge of applicable building codes and standards including IBC, ASHRAE, ASTM, SMACNA, and CSI. Project Management Manage building science & infrastructure projects from setup through completion. Coordinate project teams and direct site activities with field staff, subcontractors, and senior managers. Manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining schedule, scope, and budget objectives. Prepare and review proposals, change orders, budgets, and invoices. Monitor project progress and communicate schedule updates, testing activities, and potential budget impacts. Communicate project milestones with clients and advise on significant project changes. Client Interaction & Business Development Interface with clients regularly and lead project meetings and discussions. Present testing results, project findings, and recommendations to clients. Maintain and develop client relationships and support growth of the client database. Team Leadership & Collaboration Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams on project execution. Mentor junior staff and supervise field personnel performing inspections and testing. Coordinate staffing needs with other managers to support project execution. Documentation & Reporting Prepare building science & infrastructure reports, perform analysis, and provide recommendations. Ensure reports meet professional standards for clarity, accuracy, and technical content. Review and approve reports prepared by junior staff prior to Principal review. Additional Responsibilities Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Education & Experience Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Architectural Engineering, or Architecture (NCARB). 5+ years of related experience with building enclosure consulting, including field investigations, testing, commissioning (BECx), design review, or forensic assessments. Licensed or certified in at least one of the following preferred but not required: Professional Engineer (P.E.) Registered Architect (R.A.) IIBEC certifications (RRC, RWC, REWC, RBEC, CBECxP) University of Wisconsin-Madison certifications (BECxP, CxA+BE) Knowledge & Skills Strong knowledge of building science, building enclosure systems, and construction practices. Strong knowledge of building codes, materials, and structural or architectural systems. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong project management and consulting skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and lead multidisciplinary teams. Strong judgment, critical thinking, and decision-making abilities. Physical Requirements Ability to lift up to 40 pounds multiple times per day, stand for extended periods, walk on uneven terrain, and perform work at heights. Additional Requirements Valid driver’s license required if driving for or on behalf of an ECS subsidiary. Why Join ECS? Nationwide Building Science + Infrastructure Consulting practice made up of more than 180 employees with deep technical expertise and opportunities for collaboration across the country Opportunity to lead high-profile projects with technical complexity and visibility Be part of a growing and innovative team focused on technical excellence and client service Supportive work environment that values expertise, collaboration, and continuous learning Competitive salary, performance bonuses, and comprehensive benefits ECS is an employee-owned company with an Employee Stock Ownership program (ESOP)! 401(k) with up to 4% match Tuition Assistance Program And more! ECS Core Values: Collaborate, Focus & Lead ECS Group of Companies (ECS) was founded in 1988 with the goal to raise the standards of professional engineering consulting. Today, we are a leader in geotechnical, construction materials, environmental and building science + infrastructure consulting services. We are employee-owned with more than 3,200 employees in 125 offices and testing facilities coast to coast. ECS is currently ranked #60 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 500 Design Firms (April 2026), #144 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 200 Environmental Firms (October 2026) and #38 in Zweig Group’s Hot Firm List (June 2026). For additional information about ECS, visit: www.ecslimited.com. ECS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. To learn more, click here.

review_candidates.title: Bilingual Payroll Officer
review_candidates.description: Bilingual Payroll Officer (French and English Required) Location: Mississauga, Ontario Work Model: Hybrid, 2 days onsite every 2 weeks Schedule: 8 hours per day, with start times between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. Employment: Full-time Salary: $80,000 to $85,000 annually Languages: Strong French and English communication skills required for payroll support across Canada Work Eligibility: Legally entitled to work in Canada. Introduction Are you an experienced payroll professional who values accuracy, teamwork, and a stable work environment? Our client, an established organization in the services sector, is looking for a Bilingual Payroll Officer to join its collaborative payroll team in Mississauga. In this role, you'll manage complex, high-volume payroll across multiple provinces while supporting employees and internal departments in French and English. You'll enjoy a flexible hybrid schedule, a respectful team environment, and the opportunity to deepen your payroll expertise through varied and meaningful work. Why You'll Want This Role Enjoy a flexible hybrid arrangement with just 2 onsite days every 2 weeks. Join an experienced, supportive team that values respect, collaboration, and long-term stability. Build your expertise through exposure to complex, multi-provincial payroll, collective agreements, and varied payroll scenarios. Receive ongoing training and guidance from experienced payroll leadership. Benefit from 3 weeks of vacation, paid personal and sick days, retirement savings contributions, and additional employee benefits. What You'll Do You'll take ownership of accurate, timely biweekly payroll processing for employees across Canada, including salaried and hourly staff in unionized and non-unionized environments. You'll work independently while having access to a knowledgeable management team when complex situations require additional guidance. Your attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage competing priorities will help ensure employees are paid correctly and payroll operations run smoothly. Responsibilities Process full-cycle, high-volume biweekly payroll for employees across multiple Canadian provinces. Calculate and administer regular earnings, vacation pay, sick pay, retroactive adjustments, and other payroll transactions. Apply relevant collective agreements, payroll policies, and legislative requirements to ensure accurate calculations. Process statutory and third-party deductions, including garnishments, union dues, pension contributions, and retirement savings deductions. Respond to payroll questions from employees, site management, and internal departments in French and English. Prepare and support monthly and year-end payroll reporting, reconciliations, and regulatory filings. Use Excel to review payroll information, perform calculations, and resolve discrepancies. Maintain accurate payroll records, protect confidential employee information, and follow established internal controls. Collaborate with colleagues and management to resolve complex payroll issues and support continuous improvement. Qualifications Required: 2+ years of experience processing payroll, with a solid understanding of applicable Canadian payroll legislation and practices. Experience managing full-cycle payroll processes, including adjustments, deductions, and reconciliations. Ability to work accurately with high payroll volumes and competing deadlines. Strong French and English communication skills to support employees and internal departments across Canada. Working knowledge of collective agreements and their application to payroll calculations. Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including familiarity with VLOOKUP and PivotTables. Excellent attention to detail, discretion, organizational skills, and a customer-service mindset. Ability to work independently, take initiative, collaborate with colleagues, and seek guidance when needed. Legally entitled to work in Canada. Assets: Payroll Compliance Professional (PCP) certification or progress toward certification. Experience with cloud-based payroll or human capital management systems. Experience processing payroll across multiple provinces, including Quebec. Payroll accounting knowledge and experience supporting year-end reporting. Benefits 3 weeks of vacation, prorated during the first year. 10 paid sick days and 3 personal days. Group benefits beginning after the 90-day probationary period. RRSP matching contributions of up to 4%. Access to an onsite fitness facility and free parking. Why Work with Us At Bilingual Source, we believe the right opportunity should offer more than a new set of responsibilities. We connect bilingual professionals with organizations where their skills are valued and their contributions make a difference. Our client offers a respectful, team-oriented environment where experienced colleagues share their knowledge and employees are trusted to manage their work. If you're looking for a stable payroll opportunity with flexibility, meaningful responsibilities, and opportunities to strengthen your expertise, we'd love to hear from you. Bilingual Source uses artificial intelligence (AI) technology to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. This technology helps us match your unique language skills and professional experience with the specific needs of our clients. Final hiring and interview decisions continue to be made by our human recruitment experts. This is an existing vacancy. Our client is currently seeking a Bilingual Payroll Officer.
